questions.question: Which of the following was included by the Constitution (Eighty-sixth Amendment) Act, 2002?

options.text: Readjustment of seats of the Lok Sabha

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Elementary education as a fundamental right**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• **Right to Education **

 
 
• The **Eighty-sixth Amendment** to the Indian Constitution guarantees the **right to early childhood care until the age of six and the right to education for children aged six to fourteen.**
 
• It has replaced** Article 45 **(Early Childhood Education) of the Directive principles of State policy and has inserted Article 21A (Right to Education as a Fundamental Right) below **Article 21.**
 
• It amended **Article 51A** **(Fundamental Duties)** to add a new duty of parents to provide education to their child between the ages of six and fourteen years.
 
• Article 21A states that “The State shall provide free and compulsory education to all children of the age of six to fourteen years in such manner as the State may, by law, determine."
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• However, this right was finally implemented in 2010 after eight years.
 
• India joined a select group of nations on April 2, 2010, when a historic law declaring every child's right to education went into effect.
 
• The implementation of this was announced by former Prime Minister Manmohan Singh.
 
• Article 45 was replaced as “The State shall endeavour to provide early childhood care and education for all children until they complete the age of six years.”
 
• Article 51 states that “who is a parent or guardian to provide opportunities for education to his child or, as the case may be, ward between the age of six and fourteen years.”

questions.question: The Sub-Section (C) in the list of Fundamental Duties requires an Indian citizen to uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and ______________ of India.
The ______ was a territorial assignment given to administrative officers and nobles in lieu of the services they performed for the state during Delhi sultanate.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Iqta**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Iqta system 

 
 
• The Iqta system was a unique type of land distribution and administrative system introduced during the reign of Iltutmish.
 
• In the Iqta system the lands of the Delhi Sultanate were divided into several large and small tracts called Iqta and assigned these Iqtas to the Sultan's soldiers, officers and nobles.
 
• Iltutmish granted iqtas (land) to members of his army.
 
• Iqta is the land granted to army officials in lieu of a regular wage.
 
• The iqta holder is called the iqtadar or muqti who had to provide the Sultan with military assistance in times of war.

questions.question: Which formula is used to represent the three-dimensional structures of molecules using a two-dimensional surface like a sheet of paper or a computer screen?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**Dash-wedge formula.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The wedge and dash notation is used to represent three-dimensional structures of molecules using a two-dimensional surface, like a sheet of paper or a computer screen.
 
• This type of structure is also called **wedge-dash notation or wedges-and-dash notation.**
 
• It is commonly used in organic chemistry, though you may see it any time a molecule structure is given.
 
• **Wedges –** Solid triangular wedges represent chemical bonds and groups that are coming out of the page, toward you.
 
• **Dashes –** Dashed triangular shapes represent chemical bonds and groups extending back behind the page.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bond Line Formula:**

 
 
• A bond line structural formula is another way of structural representation of organic compounds.
 
• Here, every bond is represented as a line in a zigzag manner.
 
• If not specified, every terminal is assumed to be a **methyl (-CH3) group.**
 
 
 
• **Lewis structure formula :**
 
 
• The Lewis structure, also known as an electron fleck structure, is a diagrammatic representation of determining the total number of valence electrons present in a snippet that are ready to form bonds to form a patch and, ultimately, an emulsion.
 
 
 
• **Condensed structural formula:**
 
 
• In the condensed structural formula, every carbon atom is represented individually, and the following carbon atoms are placed to the atoms that are bonded to that particular carbon atom.

questions.question: A train crosses two persons travelling at 4 km/h and 6 km/h in the same direction in 12 sec and 14 sec, respectively. The speed of the train is ______.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a train crossing two objects in the **same direction**:

**Speed of Train (V)** = (S₂ × T₂ − S₁ × T₁) ÷ (T₂ − T₁)

V = (6 × 14 − 4 × 12) ÷ (14 − 12)

V = (84 − 48) ÷ 2 = 36 ÷ 2 = 18 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 18 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of person 1 (v₁) = 4 km/h | Time (t₁) = 12 s

Speed of person 2 (v₂) = 6 km/h | Time (t₂) = 14 s

Let the **speed of the train** be V km/h and the **length of the train** be L meters.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/980714f6d83c72578a6e15f993652599f4cfbd2d17453309f83743076de0b888.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Relative Speed × Time

Length of train (L) is constant in both cases.

⇒ L = (V − 4) × (5/18) × 12 — (i)

⇒ L = (V − 6) × (5/18) × 14 — (ii)

Equating (i) and (ii):

⇒ (V − 4) × 12 = (V − 6) × 14

⇒ 12V − 48 = 14V − 84

⇒ 14V − 12V = 84 − 48

⇒ 2V = 36

⇒ V = 18 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 18 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed Concepts

When two objects move in the **same direction**, relative speed = V₁ − V₂. When they move in **opposite directions**, relative speed = V₁ + V₂.

Unit Conversion

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

Train Crossing a Point Object

When a train crosses a pole, person, or tree, the distance covered is exactly equal to the **length of the train**.</p

questions.question: The LCM and ratio of three numbers are 1386 and 3 ∶ 7 ∶ 11, respectively. The sum of the greatest and least numbers is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of the three numbers = 3 : 7 : 11.

LCM of the ratio units = 3 × 7 × 11 = 231 units.

Common multiplier = Actual LCM ÷ LCM of units = 1386 ÷ 231 = 6.

Sum of the greatest and least numbers = (11 + 3) × 6 = 14 × 6 = 84.

**∴ The correct answer is 84.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

The ratio of three numbers = 3 : 7 : 11

The LCM of the three numbers = 1386

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/47d42f287080c1e58cdd82b6b0d7f867ab6e934ddf23ca7d1ba20c559bbc980a.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the three numbers be 3x, 7x, and 11x, where x is the common factor.

⇒ Since 3, 7, and 11 are prime numbers, the LCM of these numbers is their direct product multiplied by x.

⇒ LCM = 3 × 7 × 11 × x = 231x

⇒ 231x = 1386

⇒ x = 1386 ÷ 231

⇒ x = 6

⇒ The least number = 3x = 3 × 6 = 18

⇒ The greatest number = 11x = 11 × 6 = 66

⇒ The sum of the greatest and least numbers = 66 + 18 = 84

**∴ The correct answer is 84.**

LCM of Numbers in a Ratio

When numbers are given in a ratio and are co-prime to each other, their LCM is simply the product of the individual ratio parts multiplied by their Highest Common Factor (HCF).

HCF of Numbers in a Ratio

The common multiplier x used to define numbers from a given ratio is always the Highest Common Factor (HCF) of those numbers.

Co-prime Numbers

Numbers that share no common factors other than 1 are called co-prime numbers. For co-prime numbers, their HCF is 1, and their LCM is their direct product.
